subject: Egress policy stitching and IP ownership for private deployments
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@cedarpoint.ai>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.in
Cc: security@cedarpoint.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — outbound IPs and firewall constraints

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We're preparing our network change request and need definitive guidance from Redwood on the private deployment options so our security team can sign off. Specifically we need: 

- A concise mapping of outbound IPs (or ranges) we must allow for the control plane and data egress for a Private (VPC) deployment.
- Supported port/hostname list and whether TLS SNI is preserved when using your proxy options.
- Clarification on shared responsibility for IP rotation and the recommended approach if we require static egress IPs for regulatory reasons.
- Any required DNS entries, SANs, or certificate pins we should include.

I've attached our internal network requirements doc so you can point to where we should place exceptions. We also have a pre-scheduled change window next Wednesday (2027-08-18) and would like to finalize the allowlist by EOD Monday if possible.

Appreciate a compact action list we can hand to operations.

Thanks,
Alex Morgan
Head of Infrastructure
CedarPoint Analytics

Attachment: CedarPoint_Network_requirements_v1.pdf
From: jordan_blake@redwood.in
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@cedarpoint.ai>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.in, laura_bennett@redwood.in, aditya_rao@redwood.in
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — outbound IPs and firewall constraints

Alex —

Thanks — good to have the doc. High level: Redwood supports three primary egress patterns for Private deployments (we'll call them A/B/C below). I'll summarize the tradeoffs and provide a concrete list of what you'll need to allow. Mina and Aditya, flag any corrections below.

Summary (short):
- Pattern A: Static NAT from customer VPC (recommended where you control NAT). You get a predictable static set of egress IPs that you control; minimal changes on our side.
- Pattern B: Redwood-managed egress gateway (we provide static egress IPs). Good for customers who cannot manage NAT but needs allowlist stability — requires a peered, outbound-only connection to our gateway.
- Pattern C: On-prem proxy / TLS egress via customer proxy. Preserves SNI if configured; we can also be configured to tunnel via CONNECT for opaque destinations.

Action items for CedarPoint ops (what to allow):
- Control plane — outbound to: controlplane.redwood.in (TLS 443). If you run Private with a customer-managed control plane, this is replaced by your internal control plane hostnames.
- Runtime outbound token endpoints: token.redwood.in (TLS 443).
- Model fetch & updates: model-download.redwood-cdn.net (HTTPS 443) — allow for SNI-based CDNs.
- Telemetry/metrics (optional): telemetry.redwood.in (HTTPS 443) — can be routed through proxy.

If you want static egress IPs from our side (Pattern B), we will assign a small pool (usually /29 or /28 depending on scale). For Pattern A you own the NAT egress and rotation is on you; for Pattern B, Redwood manages rotation and will provide a maintenance schedule and an IP rotation SLA.

I've attached a compact matrix file with suggested hostnames/ports and which patterns require which entries. Mina — can you drop the CSV with the IP sets for Pattern B and notes on SNI/proxy behavior?

If this looks reasonable, happy to join your Monday operations sync (or slot a short 30m next Tue) to finalize the exact CIDRs.

—Jordan
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: mina_haddad@redwood.in
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.in>, Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@cedarpoint.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.in, aditya_rao@redwood.in
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — outbound IPs and firewall constraints

Alex / team —

Attaching the requested matrix (CSV) and adding more concrete guidance below — copied from our infra runbook but tailored to CedarPoint. Attachment: redwood-egress-ip-matrix.csv

Key points by pattern: 

Pattern A — Customer NAT (static on customer side)
- You provide the NATed static egress IP(s). Redwood runtime will appear to our public endpoints from those IPs.
- Ports: 443 (HTTPS) for all control and model traffic. We recommend also allowing outbound 53/UDP (DNS) to your resolver or Amazon/Cloud DNS if using cloud.
- Rotation: Managed entirely by CedarPoint; if you rotate, update your ops ticket and notify Redwood — we'll queue model sync windows accordingly.
- Notes: TLS SNI preserved. No Redwood IPs to allowlist.

Pattern B — Redwood egress gateway (Redwood-managed static egress)
- Redwood will provide one or more static IPv4 addresses (we prefer a /29 for small POCs, /28 for production). Example placeholders in CSV: 52.144.184.200/29.
- Ports: 443 only. We also use ephemeral TCP to our CDNs for model downloads; those flows appear from the same egress pool.
- Rotation & SLA: Redwood will provide 7-day notice before rotating IPs; for customers with stricter controls we offer an IP freeze window as part of the Dedicated contract.
- TLS: SNI is preserved for model-download and controlplane hostnames. If you require SNI-based firewall rules, allow hostnames rather than IP-only where possible.

Pattern C — Customer proxy / on-prem CONNECT
- If you route traffic through a customer-managed proxy that supports TLS CONNECT and SNI passthrough, Redwood will route model fetches and telemetry through it.
- We can be configured to behave through an authenticated proxy (basic or mTLS). For mTLS we need a client cert to be installed on our runtime — coordinate with Redwood SE.
- Ports: 3128/8080 for proxy management, but traffic ultimately egresses to 443.

Minimum allowlist (recommended for quick signoff):
- controlplane.redwood.in:443
- token.redwood.in:443
- model-download.redwood-cdn.net:443 (or allow by SNI hostnames in your appliance)
- telemetry.redwood.in:443 (optional; can be disabled)

Operational notes: 
- If CedarPoint MUST restrict by IP only, Pattern B is the fastest path to signoff — we supply the IPs and handle rotation. Expect 1–2 business day lead time to provision the pool.
- For customers on our Dedicated contract, we can add a documented IP rotation window and put rotation exceptions in the contract appendix.
- If you require RFC-compliant IP ownership proof, we can supply a signed attestation and the ASN ownership path for our egress prefixes.

Next steps I propose:
1) CedarPoint confirms which pattern you prefer (A/B/C).
2) If B, Jordan/Aditya will provision an IP pool and we provide CSV and rotation SLA.
3) Kick off a 30-min ops call to align NAT/CIDR and change window (I can join your Monday 10:00am PST slot).

—Mina
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-egress-ip-matrix.csv

Jordan / Mina —

This is perfect, thanks. CedarPoint Security reviewed the three patterns and we want to proceed with Pattern B (Redwood-managed egress) for the initial production rollout — that aligns best with our change window constraints.

Two follow-ups:
- Can you provide the actual /29 when you provision? We need the exact CIDR plus the planned rotation notice cadence to include in our change ticket.
- Please share the signed attestation for IP ownership (ASN path) per Mina's note — security will require that for audit.

We'll take the Monday 10:00am PST ops slot as proposed to finalize. I'll put a calendar invite for 30 mins.

Thanks again — looking forward to the CSV and the attestation doc.

Alex
Head of Infrastructure
CedarPoint Analytics
